citations.quote: Submit raw and derived datasets containing the core imaging facility assessments used to derive the updated response rate and median duration of **response on study** titled "A Pivotal Study of SU011248 in the Treatment of Patients with Cytokine-Refractory Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma".

design.text: Single-arm, multi-center study in patients who failed prior cytokine-based therapy (defined by radiographic disease progression per RECIST or WHO criteria); patients received 50 mg SUTENT on Schedule 4/2 until withdrawal criteria or progressive disease.

citations.quote: In Study 1, failure of prior cytokine therapy was based on radiographic evidence of disease progression defined by RECIST or World Health Organization (WHO) criteria during or within 9 months of completion of 1 cytokine therapy treatment (interferon-\alpha, interleukin-2, or interferon-\alpha plus interleukin-2; patients who were treated with interferon-\alpha alone must have received treatment for at least 28 days).
Patients received 50 mg SUTENT on Schedule 4/2. Therapy was continued until the patients met withdrawal criteria or had progressive disease.

population.text: Patients with cytokine-refractory metastatic renal cell carcinoma, all with prior nephrectomy required and histological clear-cell component required in Study 1.

citations.quote: All patients in Study 1 were required to have a histological clear-cell component.
Most patients enrolled in the studies (97% of the pooled population) had undergone nephrectomy; prior nephrectomy was required for patients enrolled in Study 1.

endpoint.text: The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR); duration of response (DR) was also evaluated.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint for both studies was ORR. Duration of response (DR) was also evaluated.
One hundred six patients were enrolled into Study 1, and 63 patients were enrolled into Study 2.

result.text: ORR (partial response) 25.5% (95% CI 17.5, 34.9), assessed by blinded core radiology laboratory; median duration of response 27.1 weeks (95% CI 24.4, *).

citations.quote: There were 27 PRs in Study 1 as assessed by a core radiology laboratory for an ORR of 25.5% (95% CI 17.5, 34.9).

target_moa.text: Sunitinib malate is a small molecule that inhibits multiple receptor tyrosine kinases implicated in tumor growth, pathologic angiogenesis, and metastatic progression, including PDGFRα and PDGFRβ, VEGFR1/2/3, KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, and RET.

citations.quote: Sunitinib malate is a small molecule that inhibits multiple RTKs, some of which are implicated in tumor growth, pathologic angiogenesis, and metastatic progression of cancer.

an inhibitor of platelet-derived growth factor receptors (PDGFR\alpha and PDGFR\beta), vascular endothelial growth factor receptors (VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and VEGFR3), stem cell factor receptor (KIT), Fms-like tyrosine kinase-3 (FLT3), colony stimulating factor receptor Type 1 (CSF-1R), and the glial cell-line derived neurotrophic factor receptor (RET).
SUTENT®, an oral multi-kinase inhibitor targeting several receptor tyrosine kinases (RTK), is the malate salt of sunitinib.
Sunitinib malate is a small molecule that inhibits multiple RTKs, some of which are implicated in tumor growth, pathologic angiogenesis, and metastatic progression of cancer.

key_safety.text: In MRCC studies (N=169), the most common adverse events (all grades) were fatigue (74%), diarrhea (55%), nausea (54%), mucositis/stomatitis (53%), hypertension (28%), and bleeding at all sites (26%). Serious risks include left ventricular dysfunction (LVEF decrease below LLN in 15% of MRCC patients) and hemorrhagic events.

citations.quote: The data described below reflect exposure to SUTENT in 169 patients with MRCC enrolled in Studies 1 and 2.

detail.text: NDA 21-968 was approved under accelerated approval regulations effective on the date of the approval letter; no prior Complete Response Letter is noted.

citations.quote: NDA 21-968 for the treatment of advanced renal cell carcinoma is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.510), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling text.

Please refer to your new drug applications (NDAs) dated August 10, 2005, received, August 11, 2005, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for SUTENT® (sunitinib malate) Capsules, 12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg.

requirement.text: Provide the response rate and duration of response data from the first interim efficacy analysis of the Phase 3 randomized study of SU011248 versus interferon-α as first-line systemic therapy for metastatic RCC, plus comparative safety data at interim data cutoff.

Also, submit the comparative safety data that are available at the time of data cutoff for the interim analysis. This will include an interim study report as well as raw and derived datasets.

requirement.text: Submit follow-up LVEF data for patients 16, 46, and 81 on the pivotal cytokine-refractory MRCC study, with case narratives and additional cardiac evaluations, plus LVEF/narratives for any patient with documented LVEF ≤ 40% and/or cardiac failure after initial data cutoff.

citations.quote: Submit follow-up left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) data for patients 16, 46, and 81 on the study titled “A Pivotal Study of SU011248 in the Treatment of Patients with Cytokine-Refractory Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma”. Case narratives should be submitted and should include additional cardiac evaluations that were performed and treatments that were administered for congestive heart failure. Additionally, submit LVEF data and clinical narratives for any patient who, after the data cutoff for the initial NDA submission, had a documented LVEF of \le 40\% and/or signs and symptoms of cardiac failure.

requirement.text: Submit comparative LVEF and cardiac safety data for patients enrolled on the adjuvant RCC trial E2805 (adjuvant sunitinib vs sorafenib vs placebo in resected RCC), with a revised protocol for ejection fraction monitoring.

The protocol will be revised to include a plan acceptable to the FDA for ejection fraction monitoring at baseline and follow-up.
